entries.boundary: MCP disconnect, malformed input or untrusted scope
limitations: Inspected official-SDK forged scope, malformed/UTF8/incomplete stdio frames, disconnect and noncooperative drain tests; host owns trusted scope and retains occupied slot until actual work drains. Optional SDK/installed stdio evidence must be separately exercised; historical report is not a fresh result.

entries.boundary: Different runtime/backend/library-tool-MCP results
limitations: Actual matrix compares direct/framework/MCP results and source identities on representative PostgreSQL lexical and Qdrant dense profiles; historical 42 retrievals/eight refusals per runtime are scoped, not every mode or current native pass.

entries.boundary: Clean install, unsupported runtime or missing optional dependency
limitations: Inspected fresh-entry-point import/I-O guards and minimal-environment resource probes. Current local artifacts are not a supported-OS/Python/Node CI matrix; V6-06 install/CI gate remains future.

entries.boundary: Migration interrupted or package rollback attempted
limitations: V6-07 release migration/rollback procedure is not yet implemented or accepted. Existing atomic storage migrations do not establish package rollback safety or restoration without revoked privileges. Do not infer completion from this audit.

entries.boundary: Held-out leakage, synthetic labels or selective benchmark reporting
limitations: Known independently pinned profiles, explicit human approval, candidate source-before-heldout decode and issued scoring path/digest guards inspected. Six recovery questions were synthetic and author/reviewer exposed; original failed run stays failed. No old heldout labels/results read for this audit.

entries.boundary: Sustained load, large inputs or too many queued requests
limitations: Inspected fixed one/two workers, one-client/one-waiter overload, queue/native cancellation and pressure guard. Node cancellation destroys client; backend may continue; immediate reuse failed and eventual bounded reuse took about 2.02 seconds with 17 refusals. No instant reuse/server-cancel acknowledgment claim.

entries.boundary: Published artifact differs from local candidate
limitations: Local archive identity and default imports are implemented; V6-08 registry publication, downloaded published-byte verification and corrective release workflow have not run. No package is claimed published.

entries.boundary: A result/embedding cache is proposed later
limitations: Architecture explicitly excludes result/embedding caching from the initial slice. No cache-hit authorization/invalidation evidence is claimed; adding a cache requires its separate scope/generation/profile tests.

entries.boundary: Approximate vector index is proposed for measured scale needs
limitations: The reference vector branch is exact search. Approximate/HNSW optimization and filtered underfill/fallback acceptance remain conditional and unimplemented; no approximate-index performance claim.

entries.boundary: Final-answer generation is added to a demo
limitations: Library outputs retrieval evidence only. No answer-generating demo or downstream unsupported-claim evaluation is implemented or accepted; citation fidelity cannot establish answer faithfulness.

entries.boundary: Stored PostgreSQL catalog-OID types prevent a hosted database upgrade
limitations: Portable lexical configuration stores names and resolves under fixed search path. Catalog/history/type checks refuse unsupported structures; historical Neon cutover is not proof for a newly upgraded target.

entries.boundary: A hosted endpoint certificate cannot be verified or plaintext startup is attempted
limitations: Explicit CA/hostname checks and encrypted/authorized native socket checks precede hosted SQL. Plaintext/certificate refusals have separate historical target evidence; no current external endpoint probe was made.

entries.boundary: A rotated database password is followed by pooler rejection and a direct network ban
limitations: Provider password rotation, cached pooled authentication and network-ban diagnosis are caller/host operations, not an automatic library recovery subsystem. Direct-target safety checks do not prove a specific remote ban/cache cause; new hosted credential intervention needs explicit bounded manual evidence.

entries.boundary: A driver returns a connection after its acquisition deadline before the timer callback runs
limitations: Inspected late-driver-return tests: absolute deadline is rechecked before yielding and the late checkout is released; acquisition timeout remains distinct from elapsed request deadline. Node socket cancellation is not remote server completion.

entries.boundary: Hosted CREATEROLE administrator cannot use DROP OWNED for a temporary runtime role
limitations: Exact fixture-owned grants/policies/roles are cleaned without DROP OWNED or broader privileges; cleanup proofs require the target-bound private journal and known graph. PostgreSQL admin cleanup is Python-owned for both native fixtures.

entries.boundary: A scoped session handle escapes its transaction, or a deadline is too large for a float
limitations: Inspected escaped/cross-task handle refusal and huge/malformed deadline tests; session/lease post-await checks prevent stale use. Callback body failures may retain explicit caller cause by design, distinct from provider/tool sanitization boundaries.

entries.boundary: A driver suppresses a rollback error or reports failed transaction exit without raising
limitations: Suppressed rollback and nonidle postconditions are tested in both runtimes; unusable clients are destroyed and cleanup failure is operational. Root native evidence is separate from these fault-injected doubles.

entries.boundary: Native text parsers disagree on CR/BOM, Unicode line boundaries, split packing or tokenizer work
limitations: Byte/digest/chunk profiles inspect CR/BOM and Unicode handling; malformed/async counter regressions reject invalid work. These are deterministic parser fixtures, not universal parser equivalence.

entries.boundary: A same-tenant caller has read scope but no document write permission
limitations: Write authorizer must return exact true before parse/lease and is rechecked for replay; role checks deny overprivileged writers and existing ACLs are retained. Application authorizer truth is a trusted boundary.

entries.boundary: COMMIT acknowledgement is lost or times out
limitations: Lost COMMIT acknowledgment tests destroy uncertain connections and do not claim no publication; recovery uses stable same intent, not blind replay. Operational failures remain distinct from missing evidence.

entries.boundary: RLS allows reading/inserting a staging generation but silently hides its ready UPDATE
limitations: Missing ready-transition row is an explicit publication barrier failure; transaction rolls back before active pointer change. Fake RLS row omission must be paired with actual native RLS evidence at checkpoints.

entries.boundary: Node returns PostgreSQL bigint/domain byte offsets as decimal strings
limitations: Node byte offsets accept only canonical safe nonnegative integer strings; malformed/boolean/unsafe driver values fail. Python numeric decoding is native; runtime precision limits remain explicit.

entries.boundary: Original source bytes differ from normalized canonical bytes, or a source budget changes during an awaited fetch
limitations: Source snapshot verifies canonical bytes/digest and snapshots byte allowance before await; opaque labels are preserved. Source truth/relevance is not established by exact source fidelity.

entries.boundary: Purge reinsertion fails, child rows are hidden by RLS, or inbound FK/trigger catalog differs
limitations: Purge validates incoming FK/internal trigger graph and exact scoped cascades; reinsertion faults restore parent/source atomically. Filtered child row counts alone do not establish deletion; external caller copies are outside library erasure.

entries.boundary: A hosted proxy terminates TLS before PostgreSQL, so backend SSL flags are false
limitations: Hosted proxy backend SSL flags are not treated as TLS proof; client encrypted/authorized/certificate hostname is checked before source SQL without exposing raw sockets in guarded API.

entries.boundary: A managed host rejects pre-hashed SQL-role passwords
limitations: Explicit Neon fixture path establishes verified TLS before its password statement; diagnostics remain safe and temporary roles cleaned. Host-managed plaintext statement mode is isolated from ordinary prehashed fixture behavior.

entries.boundary: A credential import supplies a pooled/wrong target, unsafe URI options or an existing/symlink output
limitations: Hidden-input importer pins direct host, excludes pooled/unsupported URI security options and rejects existing/symlink outputs; writes owner-only outside checkout. No credential input/output was read in this audit.

entries.boundary: Native acceptance is killed, its administrator connection is lost, or cleanup also fails
limitations: Inspected immutable exclusive private journals, target/history/ownership refusal, fresh-connector bounded retries and original-versus-cleanup errors. Missing journal cannot authorize deletion; stale native cleanup evidence requires exact identity/target qualification.

entries.boundary: Node enables ambient proxies through `NODE_OPTIONS`, rather than `execArgv`
limitations: Node explicitly scans NODE_OPTIONS and execArgv including quoted proxy flags, TLS override and ambient proxy admission before HTTP. Tests assert unsupported capability without startup-option/key text.

entries.boundary: Equal-dimensional embedding batches name another model, hide synthetic execution or lose usage
limitations: Full fixed embedding profile, immutable validated vector batch and synthetic/provider flags are checked before query. Estimated/unknown cost is not converted to known billing; fake fixtures do not establish real model quality.

entries.boundary: Canonical bytes include NUL, a mid-scalar span or invalid UTF-8 outside a valid excerpt
limitations: Python strict UTF8 decoding and Node fatal TextDecoder validate whole canonical bytes plus excerpt/mid-scalar boundaries after digest checks; SQL hashes alone are not source-release authorization.

entries.boundary: Malformed scope-grant JSON contains extreme numeric exponents or depth
limitations: scope_grants() in 0001_authority.sql:237-240 catches only declared malformed-text/Unicode/numeric-range/program-limit errors; cancellation, memory and connection failures are not caught as absent grants. Shared SQL is consumed by both runtimes; malformed exponent/depth cases need actual PostgreSQL evidence, not mocks alone.

entries.boundary: Cosine storage normalizes Float32 inputs, or two runtimes serialize floats differently
limitations: Original norm is admitted before binary32 rounding; nonfinite and nonzero underflow are rejected. Dense readback uses declared numerical equivalence, sparse content canonical exactness; arbitrary JSON hash equality is not claimed.

entries.boundary: An old worker resumes after lease expiry or an instance restart affects another document
limitations: Private proof/attempt ownership, durable blocked instance and exact key fencing exclude stale workers. Paused-supervisor native proof is historical; restart/lease/PID alone never admits successor. Automatic recovery after supervisor death is unsupported.

entries.boundary: Qdrant loads while acknowledged WAL operations are still queued for background replay
limitations: Supported single-node configuration fixes prevent_unoptimized=false and verifies recovered collection profile; status/health alone cannot settle publication or erase uncertainty. No cluster/distributed deployment profile is claimed.

entries.boundary: A valid original dense vector rounds outside the original E-r1 norm boundary, then repair restarts
limitations: Original input sidecar and private admitted vector seals survive canonical serialization/restart; boundary norm-rounding regressions ensure rounded values are not re-admitted as originals. Deserialized structural lookalikes are not issued proof.

entries.boundary: A managed writer uses a repeatable-read/serializable snapshot after waiting for an unchanged owner or generation row lock
limitations: Managed SQL explicitly demands READ COMMITTED; source readers keep separate read-only isolation. Native two-connection owner/member/gate race evidence remains historical until root reruns or verifies unchanged source/schema identity.

entries.boundary: A reserved dispatch receives more point rows after its creation transaction commits
limitations: created_xid is bound to pg_current_xact_id during reserved journal/member creation, and finite exact member count is required. Separate-commit/crash-gap native scenarios are essential; later transactions cannot append reserved membership.

entries.boundary: An internal FK trigger is disabled while constraints remain marked valid and the catalog fingerprint excludes internal trigger state
limitations: Publication structural SQL in _qdrant_authority.py:108-110 rejects every disabled trigger without the fingerprint query's NOT tgisinternal exclusion; Node embeds the matching guard. Historical native trigger-disable/unchanged-fingerprint/rollback proof must not be replaced by a catalog string test.

entries.boundary: Reader grants change after initialization, or capability membership has inheritance disabled
limitations: Each source lease rechecks effective privileges and dangerous memberships, including noninherit membership, before source byte access. Fingerprint covers structure, not effective deployment grants.

entries.boundary: Named writer capability grants, LOGIN flags or outbound memberships drift without changing the schema fingerprint
limitations: Frozen role maps check capability NOLOGIN/safe flags/outbound memberships and effective table/column/function grants each lease; tests mutate capability itself and LOGIN role, with refusal before business scope.

entries.boundary: Another publisher replaces owner and pointer while final CAS waits, or a successful older operation is retried after supersession
limitations: Fresh locked document fences precede old-owner rejection; test replaced owner/pointer and superseded completed-intent retries. Durable historical outcomes are preserved without rebasing or overwriting current pointer.

entries.boundary: A controller expects the wrong retired-key HTTP status, accepts a copied physical proof, or reopens admission after restart alone
limitations: Pinned invalid retired key requires HTTP401, fresh key actual write/readback and issuer-bound recovery proof. Copied proof or restart cannot reopen ordinary admission before durable settlement.

entries.boundary: An owned server exits, invalid recovery input arrives, or closed handles remain referenced
limitations: Supervisor checks known-dead owned child before credential/HTTP delivery, rejects invalid epoch without poisoning healthy admission and frees closed handle slots. Platform-specific controlled process profile remains a scope limit.

entries.boundary: A second manifest reuses a generation, an inner join hides an incomplete extra member, or SQL row order changes
limitations: Same generation cannot adopt changed manifest; raw bounded claim/member/journal reconstruction precedes joins and UUID order is canonical. Equal counts do not prove exact membership or complete source graph.

entries.boundary: Copied readback receipts, hidden extra points or exhausted verification bytes appear complete
limitations: Private receipt/issuer/current authority checks reject copies; readback scans complete immutable scope without profile/ID filters and shares remaining aggregate bytes through passes. Readback receipt alone cannot settle uncertainty or open admission.

entries.boundary: Two coordinators share one supervisor, or a timeout releases admission before native work unwinds
limitations: One private supervisor session spans SQL/physical/handoff; competing/nested/raw mutation and inherited/expired proof fail. Noncooperative work must drain before release; failed drain leaves durable block instead of manufacturing success.

entries.boundary: A generic lease-options helper forwards an undefined owner field into a stricter native HTTP transport
limitations: Exact HTTP options omit undefined owner metadata; strict double and native publication verification use the real transport contract. A permissive mock is not compatibility proof.

entries.boundary: A callback suppresses native cancellation and returns before the original deadline
limitations: Cancellation is latched across callback awaits and finalization; noncooperative work keeps original ownership until drain and cannot issue later SQL/HTTP. Native process authority is separate from coroutine cancellation.

entries.boundary: A publication worker loses its private channel or resumes with a retired key
limitations: Parent owns genuine supervisor, per-attempt key and IPC authority; native EOF/SIGKILL/paused-child old-key HTTP401 must corroborate doubles. Historical process evidence is not a fresh native pass.

entries.boundary: A worker/controller binding is copied or replaced, or an IPC request arrives during finalization
limitations: Private WeakKey/WeakMap registries bind exact worker/controller/channel/native objects. Tests reject copied bindings, nonterminal done, replayed IPC and operations during finalization; failed child reaping retains strong session ownership.

entries.boundary: Evaluation HTTP error bodies or exception chains contain credentials, and status failures become indistinguishable
limitations: Status codes mapped to exact auth/rate/server allowlist before response iteration; synthetic faults assert no body read, one send and no private cause/context. Failed journals remain unsealed with unknown billing; these evaluation-only guards do not imply every direct adapter sanitizes unknown caller exceptions.

entries.boundary: A trial evaluation bursts reranker calls or a pacing wait outlives the original deadline
limitations: Cohere next admission anchors at least6.1s after started operation terminal cleanup; fake productionbranch regressions cover delayedfirstdispatch, delayedclose, elapseddeadlines/cancel and finishfault. MockHTTP skips productionpacer; no distributed accountquota guarantee.

entries.boundary: A recovery packet substitutes an editable seal/path or scores labels from a different root
limitations: Known fixed paths/seal pins preserve original development prerequisite; private issued root/path/digest scoring method refuses forged/wrongroot/drift/pending approvals. Checksettings never opens heldout; source and compiled identity gates are separate. Native Node consumes label-free projection, not independent approval parser.
covered_local means implementation/test ownership inspected, not a newly executed test or native pass. No peer test/service/network/install/credential/private-config/raw-provider access.

Historical native reports retain their original source/configuration identity and scope. Root must rerun required adversarial native boundaries or explicitly verify unchanged relevant source/schema before acceptance; unit doubles alone do not prove PostgreSQL/Qdrant/process behavior.

Qdrant evidence covers pinned local single-node controlled-process profile, not clusters or all operating systems. Retired-key HTTP401, process EOF/SIGKILL, SQL isolation/member races and grant drift need actual native evidence.
Pending V6-06 CI/install matrix, V6-07 rollback procedures and V6-08 publication remain separate future gates; no full V6 or universal safety claim.
Known current-only historical candidate search, default unknown coverage/conflict miss and Node backend work after socket cancellation remain documented limits, not newly claimed capabilities.
